solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Big spenders don't text part absent member

indicators.note: absent says the following short word is missing from what came before it

blocks.note: a script is a written text
PT is the standard abbreviation for part
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A dig at lavish spenders who skip their part of a text and leave a member absent.
explanation.walkthrough: Big spenders don't is a definition by negation: the answer is the thing they never do. Member here is a parliamentary one.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to economise stingily, which is exactly the behaviour lavish people avoid, so the phrase works as a description.

clue.text: (& 27dn.) Transvestite minister to engage in country pursuit

blocks.note: in drag means dressed in clothes of the other sex
Jeremy Hunt, a Conservative cabinet minister

explanation.surface: A satirical image of a cross-dressing government minister taking up a rural sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Hunt held several UK cabinet posts; the surface pictures him in a dress on a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag hunt is a rural sport where hounds follow an artificial scent trail laid across fields instead of live quarry.

clue.text: Nick's got day off – "misfortunes"

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the short abbreviation is removed from the word before

blocks.note: Old Nick is the Devil, and the possessive adds the S
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick has had a day off and is having a run of bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is the Devil (Old Nick); DEVILS minus its D leaves EVILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Evils in the plural can mean calamities or harms suffered, the same sense as bad strokes of luck.

clue.text: One turd Nige used was a schemer

indicators.note: used in the sense of worked over or manipulated, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written; Nige is a nickname for Nigel Farage

explanation.surface: A rude jibe at Nigel Farage as a manipulative plotter.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrigue is to plot secretly, so having intrigued means having acted as a plotter or conspirator.

clue.text: Betting money on cards is a derisory toffish habit

blocks.note: a monkey is British slang for five hundred pounds, often used of a stake
a suit is a set of playing cards such as hearts or spades

explanation.surface: Gambling at cards is sneered at as a habit of the posh.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, A on B puts A above B. Habit here means clothing, as in a riding habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A monkey suit is a mocking slang term for formal evening dress such as a dinner jacket worn by the upper classes.

clue.text: (& 19dn.) In crisis no more, having come to terms with a particular sex act?

definitions.text: having come to terms with a particular sex act

blocks.note: first meaning: past the worst part of a difficulty

blocks.clueFragment: having come to terms with a particular sex act
blocks.note: second meaning: having got past a hump, which is slang for an act of sex

explanation.walkthrough: Hump is British slang both for a bad mood (having the hump) and for sex; the question mark flags the saucy reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having passed the hardest stage of a task or ordeal, so the trouble is behind you.

clue.text: Resort of alternative Labour leader with one party

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: or introduces an alternative
the opening letter of Labour
an means one
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A holiday spot favoured by a rival Labour leader and his partying friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternative Labour leader reads like a political rival, but it splits into OR and the first letter of Labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando in Florida is a famous holiday destination, home to Disney World theme parks and many tourist attractions.

clue.text: Live in Clarkson's favourite habitat? A tosser's thing

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the setting that comes after it

blocks.note: Jeremy Clarkson is a TV presenter famous for motoring shows like Top Gear
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Living in a car, the natural home of a loudmouth TV presenter, is cast as the mark of a tosser.
explanation.walkthrough: Tosser is British slang for an idiot, but here it is someone who throws the pole at Highland games.
explanation.definitionFit: A caber is the heavy tree trunk thrown in the Scottish sport of caber tossing, so it is the object such an athlete uses.

clue.text: Block Corbyn's last outburst to do some energetic vote-seeking

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the surname only

blocks.note: to bar is to block
the final letter of Corbyn
a storm is a violent outburst, as of anger

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop the latest outburst from Jeremy Corbyn, the former Labour leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To barnstorm is to tour vigorously making campaign speeches, originally in rural American towns and their barns.

clue.text: Virginia primarily underdressed in new top – for the city

indicators.note: primarily means the word that follows contributes only its opening letter
in places one piece inside the item named after it

blocks.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
N is the abbreviation for new
a top or lid is a cover
the opening letter of underdressed

explanation.surface: Virginia turns up scantily clad in a new top for a night out in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Primarily seems to go with Virginia, but VA is her abbreviation; only underdressed is cut to its first letter, which sits inside COVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver is a major Canadian city on the Pacific coast of British Columbia, so it fits the plain description.

clue.text: Terrorist organisation removing a soldier, not giving a shit routinely

indicators.note: removing says the organisation sheds the next small word from its letters

blocks.note: the Irish Republican Army
taken as written, the letter dropped
a regular is a professional soldier in the standing army

explanation.surface: A terrorist group loses a soldier and no longer cares about routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Not giving a shit reads as indifference, but it is literal: bowel movements that are not routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular describes bowels that do not move on a predictable schedule, the crude literal sense of the phrase.

clue.text: see 29ac.
Common sexual feeling with "turn-over" tongue

blocks.note: pash is informal, common slang for an infatuation or crush
TO is the standard abbreviation for turnover in sports statistics

explanation.surface: A crude crush paired with a tongue that turns over, like a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: Tongue looks like part of the kiss, but it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Pashto is a language spoken in Afghanistan and Pakistan, and tongue is a familiar synonym for language.

clue.text: Dirt rich, he's unfortunately forming a seriously racist state

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters end up in a bad order

blocks.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: A filthy-rich man unhappily building a racist regime.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of he's is a joining 'is', not part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Third Reich was Nazi Germany from 1933 to 1945, a regime built on extreme racial ideology.

clue.text: Hardly a pretty bad temper?

blocks.note: surface reading: a foul temper that is anything but attractive
setter's reading: hardly pretty describes something unattractive, and a temper is a frame of mind

explanation.walkthrough: The opposite of pretty is the first word, and temper is the second; together they make the idiom for a hostile mood.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a hostile, threatening atmosphere among people, a sullen angry state of mind shared by a crowd.

clue.text: Liberal reunion of ... just 25%

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so the letters are allowed to move

blocks.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: A Liberal party reunion draws a mere quarter of those invited.
explanation.walkthrough: Liberal looks like the political party, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-five percent is a quarter, which as a ratio is a single item out of every four counted.

clue.text: Donald Trump? Cartoon character, conservative arse

blocks.note: Pluto is Mickey Mouse's dog in Disney cartoons
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
an arse is a contemptible person, as is a rat

explanation.surface: Trump is mocked as a cartoon figure and a right-wing arse.
explanation.walkthrough: Donald suggests the Disney duck, a false trail into cartoons; the question mark marks Trump as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is someone whose power comes from great wealth, and the billionaire president is a prime example.

clue.text: see 24ac.
see 6dn.
Smell sex during off-beat DIY – steamy situation

indicators.note: off-beat means unconventional or out of rhythm, so the three letters lose their order
during puts one thing in the middle of another

blocks.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
taken as written
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A sweaty home-improvement session turns smelly and sexy.
explanation.walkthrough: DIY is do-it-yourself home repair; hum for a bad smell is British slang, and it for sex is a coy euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: Humidity is moisture in the air, which makes conditions feel steamy and damp.

clue.text: Racial element of Elisabeth – nice!

indicators.note: an element of something is a part of it, so the letters are found within the next words

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a racial element in a woman named Elisabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnic and racial are both adjectives describing groups sharing ancestry or cultural origin.

clue.text: Memorable, Nick the unknown?

blocks.note: to nick a thief is to catch them
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a mysterious man named Nick is unforgettable.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a name but is the verb meaning arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchy tune or slogan is easily remembered because it sticks in the head.

clue.text: Aid to getting your leg over is let out

definitions.text: Aid to getting your leg over

indicators.note: out suggests things put out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: Help with getting lucky sexually is released.
explanation.walkthrough: Is looks like a link but belongs to the fodder; getting your leg over is British slang for having sex, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stile is a set of steps letting walkers climb over a fence or wall, literally helping lift a leg over.

clue.text: (& 18ac.) Infamous gathering of MPs? Knock here

blocks.note: first meaning: the ... of Commons seen as having a bad name
second meaning: a knocking shop, British slang for a brothel

explanation.walkthrough: The Commons is a house and infamous means of bad reputation; knocking shop is British slang for a brothel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a euphemism for a brothel, while literally it could describe a disreputable parliamentary chamber.

clue.text: Disbanded federation's fascist organisation infiltrating old city

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force

explanation.surface: Fascists are infiltrating an ancient city in a broken-up federation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after federation is a joining 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet Union was a federal union of republics, dissolved in 1991.

clue.text: Ruthless hacking habit, maybe, appropriating truth casually

indicators.note: appropriating means taking something in, so the garment holds the other letters
casually suggests careless handling, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a hacking coat is a riding jacket, and maybe signals an example of a habit or garment
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ruthless hacker's habit of loosely appropriating the truth, maybe phone hacking.
explanation.walkthrough: Hacking suggests phone hacking by journalists, but a hacking jacket is a riding coat, and habit is clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut-throat as an adjective describes fierce, merciless competition, as ruthless does.

clue.text: see 2dn.
Hot, penetrating Annie? Large variety

indicators.note: penetrating means getting inside, so the letter goes into the show

blocks.note: Annie is a stage musical, and the question mark flags it as an example
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A sexually charged story about someone penetrating Annie, with large variety.
explanation.walkthrough: Annie looks like a woman's name but is the Broadway musical about the orphan.
explanation.definitionFit: Variety is the British name for stage entertainment of mixed acts, the kind presented in a music hall.

clue.text: (& 12ac.) Horror! Kent's got rid of queen, restored a "democratic republic"!

indicators.note: got rid of means a letter is thrown out of the combined words
restored means rebuilt, so the remaining letters are put together in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, with 's meaning has
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
taken as written, added to the fodder

explanation.surface: Kent, an English county, abolishes the monarchy and declares a republic, to general horror.
explanation.walkthrough: Restored looks like bringing back the monarchy, but it signals the rebuilding of letters. The quotation marks around the definition are ironic.
explanation.definitionFit: Its official name is the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, though it is a dictatorship, hence the scare quotes.
